area.buildings.intro: The exports, deployments and their undo, as forms. The generator itself is on the Buildings screen.
area.textures.intro: Tileable textures, AI repaint, a unit's UV atlas and its repaint by body part, LoRA datasets and training.
area.survey.intro: Measure the art of the game and of the mod, and look inside its files. Reports of a mod name its files: keep them private.
area.art.intro: Flags, icons, rings, health bars, and fixes for models and animations.
area.dev.intro: Tools for working on this program itself: sweeps, galleries, sheets, swatches, zips.
b.intro: Pick a preset, change what you like, and watch it change. Exports use Blender (the game export can do without it, experimental).
b.random.help: Random options of the current style
b.random.none: This style has no random options yet.
b.full.help: Paint the texture at its own size (up to 1024 px here) once a change settles; off: a quick 256 px preview
b.texsize: Shown at {n} px. The export paints it at the size chosen in the form.
b.p90: Buildings of class {cls} in the game: 90 % have under {p90} triangles, the largest {max}.
b.budget.help: Against what the game's own buildings of this size use
b.over: Over the budget. The owner cares about optimisation: is the extra cost worth it?
b.noblender: GLB, FBX and OBJ need Blender: install Blender 4.2 or newer, or set its path in Settings. The game export can run without it (experimental).
b.export.files.help: The model as GLB, FBX and OBJ with its texture, a .blend and three renders
b.load.bad: Those options could not be read:
b.deploy.nocopy: Set a test copy of the game in Settings to deploy into it.
b.deploy.confirm: Deploy the last game export into {copy}? Backups are kept and Undo restores the copy.
b.undo.confirm: Take the {n} deployed buildings out of {copy} and restore its files?
outputs.more: {n} files in all: Show in folder for the rest.
jobs.intro: Every task started in this session, with its log.
tool.trial.help: The trial shows what would change. Apply runs it for real, once a trial with the same values has passed.
tool.apply.confirm: Apply the changes the trial showed?
settings.intro: Where things are. Nothing here leaves this computer.
settings.engines.help: Blender is needed for the game export, the GLB/FBX/OBJ export and renders; ComfyUI for the AI tasks; the Granny bridge for compressed game models.
eng.python.detail: built in: previews, sheets, every tool without Blender
eng.bpy: the bpy module of this Python
set.game.help: The game's installation. The studio only reads it, never writes into it.
set.mod.help: The mod's own folder, to survey its art.
set.test_copy.help: A copy of the game to deploy into and test. A Steam folder is refused.
set.work.help: Where the studio writes what it makes, unless a task says otherwise.
set.cache.help: Caches of game files (uncompressed models), outside the game and outside this program.
set.blender.help: blender.exe. Empty: the newest installed Blender is found by itself.
set.granny.help: The external .exe that reads compressed models through the game's granny2.dll. Not shipped with the studio.
set.comfy_url.help: The address of ComfyUI, for the AI tasks.
set.comfy_dir.help: The ComfyUI folder (ComfyUI_windows_portable), to train LoRAs.
i.title: Look inside a game file
i.intro: A texture (.ddt), a model (.gr2), a compiled XML (.xmb) or an archive (.bar): read only, nothing is written.
i.binary: A binary file of {n} bytes: its first bytes.
i.more: The first 500 shown: filter to find the others.
i.texture.none: Its texture is not beside it: shown in clay.
r.title: Repaint a unit
r.intro: A unit's texture repainted part by part: pick the islands of its UV map on the picture, add paint steps, watch the unit change, then write the texture as the game reads it.
r.model: The model (.gr2, uncompressed or with the cache)
r.scale.help: Paint a small texture at 2 or 4 times its size
r.nogame: Set the game's folder in Settings, or load a model file.
r.howto: Click an island to add it to the step selected (Ctrl or Alt: to take it out); a part's button adds the whole part; Shift and drag draws a box. Double-click the picture to fit it.
r.part.add: Add this part to the step, or take it out
r.where.none: nowhere yet: click islands or parts
r.where.pc.help: Where the starting texture shows the player colour
r.ai.note: The AI step runs when the texture is written (it needs ComfyUI): the preview leaves it out.
r.box: {box}: Shift and drag on the picture to place it
r.ai.skipped: {n} AI step(s) left for the writing.
r.name: Name
r.write.help: Into {folder}, with the recipe, the atlas and a sheet of before and after.
part.head: Head
r.empty: Step {steps} paints nowhere yet: click islands or parts.
f.title: Design a civ flag
f.intro: One picture of the flag becomes the whole set the game shows: the flag over buildings, the postgame flag, the buttons in their four states. Made as the game copy's own sets are, seen as you go.
f.crop.help: Shift and drag on the picture to use only a part of it. Hoist on the left.
f.name: Name
f.write.help: Into the work folder, laid out like the copy's art folder, with a preview sheet. Nothing is written into the copy itself.
x.title: Make a tileable texture
x.intro: From a photograph: pick the square to use, see it made seamless and de-lit at once, tiled 3 by 3 and measured against the mod's own textures; keep it in the library, and the buildings can paint with it.
x.photo.help: or drop it here; Shift and drag on it chooses the square
x.sheet: Tiled 3 × 3: the joins and anything that repeats
x.light.help: Divide out the photograph's broad light and shade
x.fit: Bring it to the mod's grain and colour
x.fit.help: Its grain and saturation moved to the median of the mod's own textures of this kind
x.seam: Join across the edges: {before} in the photograph, {after} in the texture (about 1 tiles unseen).
x.against: Against {what} ({n} textures), in widths of their middle half:
x.distance.help: 0 is the mod's median; within 0.5, as most of its textures; beyond 1, well outside.
x.name: Name
x.keep.help: The licence is kept beside the texture: a photograph carries the rights of whoever took it.
x.use.help: The buildings' previews and exports in this studio paint with the textures that have a style and a role (Material swatches on)
x.delete.confirm: Delete {name} from the library? Its picture and notes are removed.
a.title: AI repaint, region by region
a.intro: The local ComfyUI repaints each region chosen, keeping its layout, its edges and the player colour; the model shows each one as it is done.
a.nocomfy: Needs ComfyUI running (its address is in Settings).
a.noprompt: no prompt for it: left as painted
a.guard.help: A region whose windows or rows moved is repainted lighter, or kept
a.used: The export will use this texture.
a.in.export: The export uses the AI repaint (a change to the building drops it).
b.check.help: The game-ready checks of the add-on (needs Blender, a few seconds)
b.check.title: Checks
b.check.old: (of an earlier version of the building)
s.title: Prop set
s.intro: Several props as one unit of the game: its models are the variations the map shows, all on one texture.
s.info: {n} variations, {tris} triangles in all, one texture of {px} px.
c.nodir: Set the ComfyUI folder above first
c.starting: ComfyUI is starting in its own window: check it in about 20 s.
c.ready: ComfyUI is ready: every node and model the repaints need is there.
log.title: The studio's log
log.help: Errors and tasks are kept in the log: send it with a report when something goes wrong.
offline.help: Its window was closed, or it stopped: open AoE3 Mod Studio again (this page comes back by itself if it starts on the same address).
w.title: Welcome to AoE3 Mod Studio
w.intro: Make buildings, textures, flags and more for Age of Empires III mods. A few folders open everything; much already works without them.
w.ready.buildings: The building generator, with its 3D preview and technical sheets
w.ready.textures: Tileable textures from photographs, and the texture library
w.ready.exports: Exports to the game and to GLB, FBX, OBJ (Blender found)
w.ready.exports.no: Exports need Blender 4.2 or newer: install it from blender.org, the studio finds it
w.ready.ai.no: AI repaints need ComfyUI running: optional, see Settings
w.folders.help: Each one is checked as you choose it. Nothing is ever written into the game's own folder.
w.why.game: Your game: to survey its art, find its units for repainting and measure its flags. It is only read.
w.why.test_copy: A copy of the game made for testing (not the Steam folder): your buildings are deployed there, and taken out again.
w.why.mod: Your mod's own folder, to measure its art so new work matches it.
w.why.comfy_dir: The ComfyUI folder (ComfyUI_windows_portable), to start it from here for the AI repaints.
w.n.no_art: No art folder: is it the game's (or mod's) folder?
w.n.no_data: No data folder: is it the game's folder?
w.n.steam_refused: This is a Steam folder: the studio never writes there. Make a copy for testing.
w.n.steam_read_only: The Steam folder: fine, it is only read
w.n.comfy_not_portable: No portable ComfyUI there (python_embeded and ComfyUI\main.py)
w.n.same_as_game: The test copy must not be the game itself
f.find.help: Look in the copy's art for the folders that hold flag sets
f.find.none: No flag sets found in that copy's art
b.v.person.help: A person 1.8 m tall beside the building, for its scale
b.v.obstruction.help: The ground the building blocks in the game (from its technical sheet)
b.v.lowpoly.help: The model the game draws at its low detail setting
b.v.damaged.help: The texture the game shows once the building has lost hit points
b.v.team.help: The player colour seen in this team's colour (with Player colour on)
b.deploy.empty: Nothing of ours is deployed in it yet.
b.deploy.add.help: Add: the new building joins the others; Undo takes them all out together.
b.deploy.update.help: Update: the {n} others are deployed again with the new version of this one.
b.deploy.missing: {n} of the others' bundles are no longer on disk: they cannot be deployed again, so only Replace is possible.
b.deploy.replace.help: Replace all: the {n} buildings deployed now are taken out, and only this one stays.
r.missing: Step {step} skips what this unit has not: {why}.
b.more.help: The settlement composer, and the buildings' forms: exports, deployments, undo
se.title: Compose a settlement
se.intro: Units laid round a socket as the mod's own settlements are (distances, counts and a free lane, measured on its groupings), seen from above. Move and turn them, then write the grouping file and deploy it to the test copy.
se.verify: To verify in game: which way the game's x and z run on this plan, and which way a unit faces. Here x runs right, z up, and a line shows each unit's facing.
se.units.help: One line per unit: its class, its proto name, how many variations its set has, and its footprint's radius in game units.
se.obstruction.none: none (the proto of an invisible obstruction)
se.counts: How many of each (empty: the mod's median)
se.name: Name
se.deploy.help: Opens the grouping deployment form with this file and the test copy
se.saved: Grouping written in the work folder.
se.none: Lay a settlement out, or open a grouping.
se.select: Click a unit on the plan to move it, turn it or change it.
se.keys: Drag to move; the wheel, or Q and E, turn it by 15°; Delete removes it.
rs.title: A survey's results
rs.intro: What a texture or model survey measured, as a table: every group with its quartiles, shares and palette, sorted by any column.
rs.filter: Filter by origin, category, role or material
b.noblender.help: The game bundle made by this program alone: the same textures, anim file and proto as Blender's, the same mesh seen at any angle, icons from its own renderer. Whether it looks the same in game is still to verify.
h.title: Game interface
h.intro: The in-game HUD of your game copy as the game draws it: the main screen and its panels, normal or minimised, at any screen size and culture. Choose a gadget on the picture or in the tree to see everything it says.
h.assumed: What the engine does that the files do not say (to verify in game)
h.pick: Choose a gadget on the picture or in the tree. Drag it to move it (with its children; Alt: alone), its corners to resize it; arrows nudge it (Shift: 10). The middle or right button moves the view; the wheel zooms.
h.nofont: {f}: not in fonts3.xml (what the game draws is to verify)
h.nogame: Set the game's folder in Settings: its interface is read from there (never written).
h.r.nostring: not in the string table; the game shows “{fallback}”
h.r.notex: not in this copy: nothing is drawn
h.r.unknownfn: a name this program does not know
h.r.stub: Always empty in the stock game.
h.r.outside: It lies outside its parent's box: drawn, but it shows and hides with that parent.
h.u.search: Find a unit or building of this copy
h.u.aura: Under one of the DLL's auras
h.u.keys: The DLL's keys ({n} in this copy)
h.u.dll: uhc.dll is in this copy; its keys are read from {files}. Switching one on here only simulates it.
h.u.nodll: This copy has no uhc.dll: no row of the DLL shows.
h.u.norows: No rows file at {path}: choose one to see what it would show.
h.u.absent: Exists, but this unit does not show it ({n})
h.why.ui_variant: The minimised UI has no such row; the normal UI shows it.
h.why.not_unit: Only for units of type Unit (a building never shows it).
h.why.no_data: This unit has no such data.
h.why.no_room: No room: the minimised panel shows {MIN} attack rows ({row} is left out).
h.why.one_of: The game shows one of them.
h.why.dll_absent: uhc.dll is not in this copy.
h.why.key_off: The key {key} is not in a Startup .cfg.
h.why.not_placed: No row of the rows file places it (it is also the text {ref}).
h.why.gadget_missing: Its row names the gadget {gadget}, which this copy's layout does not have.
h.why.parent_hidden: Its gadget {gadget} hangs from {parent}, which the file hides.
h.why.needs_key: It needs the key {keys} as well.
h.why.type_not_in_key: The key {key} does not list this unit's types.
h.why.needs_state: It shows only while the unit is so (see 'What it is doing').
h.why.live_only: Only known while a game runs.
h.why.unknown_item: An item this program does not know.
h.en.editor: (add it with the editor: next version)
h.u.items: Each item and what else it needs ({n})
h.why.only_common: Nothing else: only what is said above.
h.u.nounits: This copy has no units to show (no data\protoy.xml?).
h.edithelp: Edits change only what they touch; the rest of each file stays as it is, byte for byte.
h.saverefused: The check found errors (a gadget the game fills was taken out, or a rectangle it cannot read). Save anyway?
h.f.none: Nothing to say: the edits look sound.
h.f.engine_gone: {name}: the game fills this gadget by its name; renamed or deleted, its row disappears.
h.f.duplicate: {name}: another gadget has the same name now.
h.f.outside: {name}: outside its parent's box (it shows and hides with that parent).
h.f.font_missing: {name}: {font} is not in fonts3.xml (it will be drawn as the fallback).
h.f.texture_missing: {name}: the texture {path} is not in this copy.
h.f.string_missing: {name}: the text $${id}$$ is not in the string table.
h.f.xmb_twin: A compiled twin is beside it ({path}): the game may read that one; take it away when you deploy.
h.f.row_without_gadget: The DLL's row {name} names a gadget the layout does not have.
h.nopanel: This layout has no unit selection panel to put a row in.
h.pickmore: Choose two gadgets or more (Shift + click).
h.arrangehelp: Choose gadgets with Shift + click; the one chosen last is the guide.
h.staticons.help: Draw new stat icons for the rows (the stat icons form)
h.picktex: Choose a texture of this copy
h.deploysure: The saved files go into {copy}: what they replace is backed up, a compiled twin is taken out, and Undo the deployment puts everything back. The game's own folder is never touched.
h.deploying: Deploying: the task's log shows each file.
h.nocopy: Set a test copy in Settings to deploy it there.
h.undohint: To take it out again: Buildings › Settlements and more forms › Undo the deployment.
m.title: Your own model
m.intro: A static model you made (.obj, .glb, .gltf) as a game building or prop, without Blender: seen beside a person, checked, then exported.
m.path.ph: An .obj (its .mtl and picture beside it), a .glb or a .gltf
m.fit.help: The plot's longer side, in game units (4 for the 4x4 class); empty: the scale decides
m.none: Choose a model file to see it.
m.noextras: An imported model has no low-poly or damaged variant and no technical sheet: those come from the generator.
m.name: Name (letters, digits, _)
i.bone.help: Colour the vertices by this bone's weight (blue none, red all); again to clear
i.bind.ok: Its rest pose is its bind pose: the game's animations of these bones fit it.
i.bind.no: Its rest pose differs from its bind pose in some bone: its own animations are needed (to verify).
i.skin.help: {n} bones move vertices (the number beside each); up to {most} bones a vertex. Choose a bone to see its weights.
a.lora.help: A LoRA of ComfyUI's models/loras to paint with, e.g. one trained on the game's or the mod's textures (tools/train_lora.py). Empty: none.
